transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-09
Start: 14:30 PDT
Duration: ~60m
Attendees: Lena Alvarez (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Kim (Polaris Head of Partnerships), Derek Zhou (Polaris Cloud Architect), Priya Rao (Polaris Security PM)

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda — marketplace listing status, reference arch, networking/peering, SSO/KMS, and test plan. Is that right Marta?
[00:12] Marta: Yep that's perfect. We wanna make sure the listing aligns with Polaris marketplace requirements and the joint-solution page is accurate.
[00:20] Ravi: I'll focus on the technical flow; Lena will handle the go-to-market / listing aspects.
[00:27] Derek: Quick note, our infra team is strict about VPC peering and egress. We'll need concrete CIDRs and a minimal set of allowed egress to pass our security gate.
[00:38] Priya: And from security we need SAML metadata, KMS key wrap details, and audit log retention specifics. SOC2 scope will matter for the reference arch.
[00:50] Lena: Understood. On the listing side, we have the template from Polaris marketplace — short blurb, features, pricing tiers, and joint logos. I'll draft that and share.
[01:05] Ravi: For the reference arch, I'm proposing three deployment patterns: 1) Hosted Redwood (Redwood-hosted inference) for fastest onboarding, 2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) for predictable throughput and tenancy, and 3) Private/VPC-backend for regulated customers. Each will have slightly different network and KMS flows.
[01:25] Derek: Can you show a diagram or call out the network flow for the private option? I need to see how the VPC peering or VPC endpoint would look.
[01:35] Ravi: Sure, high level — Polaris VPC peering or AWS Transit with a dedicated Redwood subnet. For private, we recommend setting up a private endpoint and route table rules; KV cache stays in Redwood runtime but can be disabled if required. There may be a small cost delta for dedicated peering.
[01:58] Marta: Will that require opening wide egress to public internet? Our security team won't like that.
[02:05] Ravi: Not necessarily. For private deployments we can establish VPC peering and keep traffic over AWS backbone. For hosted customers we do egress but we offer encryption in transit and at rest. There are tradeoffs.
[02:20] Priya: How does KMS integration work? We need to ensure customer-managed keys or CMKs are supported for private deployments.
[02:30] Ravi: We support KMS/HSM integrations in Private mode — you can bring your own CMK. For Dedicated, we can support a customer-managed key; for hosted there are options but with different audit boundaries. I'll note this in the reference arch doc.
[02:48] Derek: Also need to confirm SAML single sign-on for the console so our ops team can access logs and dashboards.
[02:55] Lena: We support SSO via SAML/SAML2.0 and we can set up a service account for logs push. We'll include sample metadata in the doc.
[03:08] Marta: Marketplace listing question — pricing. Polaris typically wants a per-hour listing and a note around data residency. Can Redwood provide a recommended set of SKUs?
[03:20] Lena: Yes, we'll propose three SKUs: 'Hosted pay-as-you-go', 'Dedicated reserved (monthly commit)', and 'Private licensing'. I'll add estimated unit economics and point to Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization to improve cost.
[03:37] Derek: On testing — we'd like to run a validation test that includes a representative workload: 100 concurrent requests with 512 token contexts, and measure tail latency. Is Redwood able to run that in a staging environment?
[03:50] Ravi: Absolutely. We can run benchmarks in a Polaris staging account or in a Redwood sandbox that mirrors your config. We'll need the staging VPC details and service account creds.
[04:02] Priya: We also need to capture audit logs for requests and token-level cost details for billing reconciliation. Does Redwood expose token-level cost and raw traces?
[04:12] Ravi: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost breakdowns and tracing hooks. We can send a sample dashboard link.
[04:22] Marta: Nice. Any competitor concerns? Polaris was evaluating CloudPeak and AuroraCloud earlier.
[04:28] Lena: We're aware. Our differentiators for the listing: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, explicit RU and latency numbers on our catalog, and the cost-performance toolset.
[04:40] Derek: For network specifics — I'll provide our staging CIDRs and SAML metadata. Also need to know what ports/protocols the Redwood runtime requires outbound.
[04:51] Ravi: We'll include a minimal port list: TLS outbound to Redwood control plane, gRPC/TCP for inference egress if applicable. We'll put exact port numbers in the infra appendix.
[05:05] Priya: Regarding audit and retention — we require 1 year of request logs for now, possibly longer for some customers. Can Redwood support configurable retention?
[05:15] Ravi: Yes, retention options are configurable in Private and Dedicated deployments; hosted has standard retention but add-ons exist. We'll document options and costs.
[05:28] Lena: Great. To recap next steps — I'll share the marketplace draft and pricing; Ravi will prepare the reference arch diagram and infra appendix; Polaris to share staging VPC info and SAML metadata. We'll run a staging benchmark once artifacts are shared.
[05:45] Marta: Sounds good. Can we get the first drafts by Friday?
[05:50] Lena: Yes — I'll send the draft by Friday (2026-06-12).
[05:55] Derek: We'll try to provide CIDRs and SAML by Tuesday (2026-06-16).
[06:00] Lena: Thanks everyone, we'll recirculate notes and action items.

End of transcript.
